title: SLI assembly and rotational fallback orchestration for endpoints
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define a reproducible, per-endpoint SLI synthesis method and an orchestration policy we call 'rotational fallback' to proactively move traffic between compatible model variants/regions when capacity or quality risk is detected. The goal is to reduce user-visible outages and noisy degradation while keeping error-budget accounting auditable at tenant and route granularity. This ticket covers: SLI composition rules, sliding-window circuit-breaker thresholds, error-budget escrow for canaries, rotational fallback scheduler semantics, eviction backoff, and the observability/dashboarding and runbook items needed for safe rollout.
updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with reliability, serving, and console teams. Align on goals: provide a single per-endpoint SLI value used for policy gating and SLO reporting.

2025-02-14: Proposal v1 drafted — composite SLI = 0.6 * availability + 0.3 * quality_score + 0.1 * latency_tail_score (normalized). Shared doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SLI+Synthesis+Proposal
2025-02-16: Engineering review feedback: request-type bucketing required (chat vs. completion vs. embed), add tenant-weighted burn-rate, and ensure KV-cache hit rate is a modifier not primary metric.

2025-02-17: Implemented prototype aggregator in telemetry pipeline (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423). Aggregates per-route quantiles and synthetic-promptset quality probes every 60s.

2025-02-19: Draft rotational fallback orchestration design posted. Key idea: allocate short timeslices (30s) to candidate fallback variants in a round-robin weight-preserving schedule to avoid single-variant overload. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Rotational+Fallback+Design

2025-02-20: Safety constraints added: error-budget escrow (5% of daily budget) reserved for canary traffic and critical tenants; circuit-breaker uses Poisson-adjusted thresholds over a 5m sliding window. Preparing runbook and dashboards for initial rollout in staging.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible SLI value exists per endpoint computed in the telemetry pipeline and visible in Grafana per-route dashboard
Circuit breaker evaluation library integrated in runtime with configurable thresholds and a unit-tested Poisson-adjusted threshold calculator
Rotational fallback scheduler implemented in the orchestration layer with traffic-slice metrics and tenant-priority honoring
Error-budget escrow mechanism implemented and visible in console; can be used to permit canary ramps without affecting tenant budgets immediately
Runbook completed: decision matrix, escalation contacts, rollback steps, and postmortem template included
Staging rollout completed with at least 48h of monitoring and two simulated region degradation tests without customer-facing errors
